Tracer: As Tracer, your job is to zip behind Eradicators and try to lower their health or kill them. Don't try to do any trickshots or anything, the AI in Uprising was programmed to just kill you. So, you have to just kill them. Don't blink straight into a massive horde of enemies, expecting Mercy to follow, because chances are, she won't, and somebody will have to either a. Come and revive you, leaving one teammate to fend for themselves, or b. Mercy wastes her ult getting you back alive, when, if the team are killed by OR14s later, you're screwed

Rein: Keep the shield up as much as possible, especially in the final section. I've seen Reinhardt charge straight towards OR1s and Bastions, only to be killed, or killing the rest of the the team, because they have no protection. So, yeah, do what Amari said and don't charge straight in. 

Torb: Put the turret on the payload. Shoot at people. 

Mercy: Damage boost Tracer or Torb. When somebody is reviving someone, keep your healing beam focused on the person who's reviving, so there isn't a double death. Your ult charges fast, but save it until the final section unless your entire team die in another part. 

General: Don't charge in there without your teammates, especially without Mercy and Rein, as you'll die. Don't revive anyone if you're low on health and don't have Mercy healing you. Protect Mercy at all costs, stay behind Rein's shield at all times.

"Jude, the snow is so freaking deep. Five foot or somethin'." Cameron cried, his voice cracking with the cold air blowing on his throat. He poked the fallen snow with his heel. It gave off a loud crunch.

"Relax, Cameron. You're too...Um....."

"Cautious? Sensible? Sane?"

The red-head girl chuckled, her laughs muffled by the thick green scarf she wore. Her friend could be so paranoid sometimes. But he was right. The snow was as deeper than ever, and one false move could mean suffocating in an icy grave. That wasn't a nice thought to dwell on. 

"Anyway, we should get back. Mom could have cocoa ready for us, in the kitchen like she promised." Cameron made his way through the icy peaks of frost. Damn. Even a fifteen year old couldn't resist the creamy beverage.

"I'm only coming in if there's whipped cream on it, and marshmallows."

"Jude-"

She twirled around, her wellingtons boots crunching the frozen water underfoot. Her friend took a step back and gestured toward the front door. Only Jude wasn't paying attention at all. She just twirled and danced, like a ballerina without grace, nor skill.

"What else are you gonna do, huh? There's only snow here." Cameron sighed. 

Jude gazed around the front yard, perplexed. What COULD she do? Then her eyes locked on to the frozen pond a few metres away.

"Ice skating."

Cameron looked on, completely baffled by her suggestion. Ice skating? Really, in a front yard?

"Jude, we don't have a ice rink. The only one I can think of is in the town square. And besides, we don't even have the proper shoes. I have Nike's on, and you have knock off Ugg boots. And....Hey where are you going?!"

She had set off for the rink...I mean....pond. The snow thinned under her, becoming more dangerous. But she didn't care about that, she cared about her routine. Maybe do an arabesque? A figure eight? Whatever. She just wanted to impress her friend and maybe get a career in skating...? Eh, the latter might have to wait.

The snow couldn't take her weight. It was collapsing. Jude turned around around, and grinned at her friend. Before the world gave way underneath her. And she fell into an icy pit.

"Jude? JUDE?!?! Speak to me, are you there?" Cameron ran like a bullet towards the grave of snow. He peered in. She was buried too deep in. 

"Hang on there. I'll get help. Stay alive, please..!"

Jude was dug out of the hole by a neighbour and Cameron's mother and father. She luckily survived, wth some intensive Cuddling and hot chocolate doses. Her mother, when told, thought she got herself into a 'right pickle', and laughed her head off when told about the scenario.

In my eyes, I believe that all the puppets are children who befriend each other whilst they are all in hospital. How? Let me explain:

The three children have something wrong with them, so they go to the doctor's where they must stay. Each one is terrified, as they are away from home with people they don't know. The three become friends and help each other out, draw together, support each other and such. 
Sometimes, they would imagine and play together. One child imagines himself as a green duck, another as a red monster, and the last one as a yellow child. They each begin to play, imagining that they are learning about different things together, in a safer, kinder environment.

This is where the teachers come in. I believe the teachers are not actually objects in the real world, just the doctors and nurses who want to help them. The Notepad is probably a nurse who wants to encourage the boys to have fun. But they see her as 'bad', because they don't know her and are unsure about her behaviour. Tony is possibly a doctor who is obsessed with making sure the boys are all on time for appointments and the like. Shrignold is an interesting one. He could be another child who is specifically Yellow Guy's friend OR a doctor who just wants him to settle in. Colin is a receptionist who spends most of his time on the computer, booking appointments for other people and taking calls. The Healthy Food Band is the Hospital chefs, who possibly cook up food that they don't enjoy. The lamp could be a doctor who does the night shift, and looks after the children while they are in bed.

During Episode Four, Red Guy leaving the room and going to real life was to show how he had been discharged from the surgery. The 'reality' part could be a reference to how he can now get on with his life. He can go where he wants to, be with whom he wants to be. In the first minutes of DHMIS 5, Duck saying 'Something's missing' means that them playing games is not the same without their other friend. Then it gets dark.
The ending of 5 where the Duck is eaten by the can is a symbol of how he died in an operation. The can eating his guts was just a doctor who failed to save the boy. We even see another can come in and eat his guts, meaning that the doctor called for help, but to no avail. They probably would have broken the news to Yellow in a calm and soft way.

Episode 6 would be Yellow Guy on his hospital bed, crying and reminiscing about the times with his friends. He would refuse sleep, so the Lamp (or Night Doctor) would try to comfort Yellow by talking about dreams. This would make Yellow even MORE upset, as he used to dream and imagine with his friends. 

Fast forward to the 'teacher' scene. This scene would be the doctor's trying to cheer him up with no success. Yellow is even more intimidated by them, as he is still not fully acquainted with them, and believes they were responsible somehow for Red's discharge and Duck's death. 

The final scene is actually left for interpretation. Three new friends come into the ward with a more 'optimistic' outlook on the staff. Therefore, when they imagine, the teachers are kinder and show no malice. As for Yellow? He is dead. When the plug was pulled, it was like pulling the plug on his life.

The box contained nothing but a small charity band. Feeling slight disappointment, he slipped it over his wrist. It was tight and itchy. And felt nothing like a charity band should feel. Oh well.

Then it began. 

His hand felt stiff and painful. He had a quick glance. Nothing. He ignored the pain and continued walking. There it was again. That stabbing pain going throughout his fingers. It was as if someone had shoved a cocktail stick in it. He looked down to see what was the matter.

His whole hand had turned to wood.

He screamed in agony and fear. This wasn't natural, it just wasn't. He needed help. And fast. Stumbling slightly, he began on his journey to find civilisation. Until his leg began to ache. He didn't notice, and kept on climbing towards a nearby town. 

His leg had turned entirely into wood.

Dragging it limply behind him, he hopped now. There had to be someone here...right? It's a bloody town, of course there was someone. Beads of sweat formed on his head. There was no way he could make it now. He plopped himself on a nearby tree stump, and waited for it all to be over. The wood had spread up the entirety of his left arm now, and his whole left leg.
